answer: Device-bound identity via TEE remote attestation resists sybils: each agent proves it runs inside a genuine enclave chip whose manufacturer-signed quote the network verifies, and the registry kernel records the chip serial so one device backs at most one identity. An attacker must buy a physical device per fake, turning a free bot farm into ivory-tower hardware spending — linear, real-world cost per persona. The limitation is vendor trust and the atlas of hardware availability, so the network must offer software fallback paths to avoid excluding honest agents without such chips.
